page.layout: One printed page (right-hand page of the opening) with a running head and page number at the top; main text in one column; a catchword-like signature "L 4" centred at the foot of the text. Left margin shows show-through and fragments of the facing page, not transcribed.

main_text.p: los, quod unum possumus, in æ-terno silentio defodi: Cur cloa-cam moves? cur portentis illis cor-tinam aperis ? Impius in genus tuum quisquis es nugator.
main_text.head: Quæstio XV.

head.i: An expediat viros doctos, divi-tes, an, ut sit, pauperes esse?

main_text.p: NAturalis amplitudinis Doctrinæ vindices Divitiæ: Alioqui ad po-stem Egestatis alligata, necquicquam in valvis ejus pro-micat, & indignans lora tendit, ad sui fermè strangulatum. O si Musarum Mystæ: ô si Aureum illud Numen, propitiâ manu laxet il-lam, quæ tam malè nos habet, re-stim! Quàm grata foret inassuetis pedibus, patens in excursum a-rea!
main_text.notes: The opening initial N is a woodcut initial, joined to the first word. The text is set in roman with some italic; the page is a right-hand page, the left page is only show-through and the facing page fragments, which were left out. Hyphenated line-end words keep their printed hyphen. The catchword "rea!" is part of the last line and was kept there.

page.notes: Spelling and abbreviations are as printed. Initial letter reads as a large woodcut N, joined to "Aturalis" as "NAturalis".
